message.content: The codebase uses lowercase comments with square-bracket annotations to enforce a consistent, machine-parseable style across the Perl-based multi-agent system. Lowercase comments (e.g., `## read config ##`) avoid header confusion since Perl keywords like `use`, `require`, and `sub` are already lowercase — using uppercase would risk collision with reserved words or make it harder to distinguish documentation from code. Square-bracket annotations (e.g., `[ module.name ]`) serve as structural markers that machines can reliably parse to identify module boundaries, function scopes, and section headers. This convention, combined with the dot-notation naming scheme (e.g., `zenka.subsystem.function`), creates a predictable, machine-readable format that simplifies automated parsing, linting, and code generation within the P7 system.
